simple.meaning: עֲרָבִי (ʻĂrâbîy) appears 10 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with flocks and in connection with kingship. The surrounding account also brings the name into conflict.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 2 Chronicles, Nehemiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at 2 Chronicles 17:11. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, flock, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲרָבִי (H6163) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows עֲרָבִי through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: עֲרָבִי (ʻĂrâbîy) / H6163 is tracked through 2 Chronicles 17:11, 2 Chronicles 21:16, 2 Chronicles 22:1, 2 Chronicles 26:7. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat presents and silver for tribute. The Arabians also brought him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams, and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
Yahweh stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians who are beside the Ethiopians;

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, because the band of men who came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the oldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and the Meunim.
God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and the Meunim.

But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they ridiculed us, and despised us, and said, “What is this thing that you are doing? Will you rebel against the king?”
But when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was angry, and was very indignant, and mocked the Jews.

Now when it was reported to Sanballat, Tobiah, and to Geshem the Arabian, and to the rest of our enemies, that I had built the wall, and that there was no breach left in it (though even to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates)
It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian will not pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make their flocks lie down there.

“Lift up your eyes to the bare heights, and see! Where have you not been lain with? You have sat waiting for them by the road, as an Arabian in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your prostitution and with your wickedness.

definitions.short: an Arabian or inhabitant of Arab (i.e. Arabia)
definitions.full: H6163. Arabiy עֲרָבִי name, of a people of foregoing, steppe-dweller ; — Isa 13:20 ; ׳כַּעֲרָבִ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר Jer 3:2 . עַרְבִי adjective, of a people Arabian (in strictly ethnographic sense, Nö l.c .); — ׳הָע as substantive Neh 2:19 Geshem the Arabian , so 6:1 ; plural הָעַרְבִים 4:1 ; 2Chr 21:16 ; 22:1 ; also (written as Late Hebrew) הערביים 26:7 (Qr הָעַרְבִים ), and even הָעַרְבִיאִים 17:11 .
